title: Причина ссоры Насти с отцом  (The Reason Behind Nastya's Feud with Her Father)

segments.t: Noticing that Nastya is upset after her mother's visit, Kostya asks why she and her father had such a bitter falling-out in the first place. Nastya flashes back to the day she told her parents she hated meat, only for her sausage-factory-owner father to tell her that every ruble she owned came from cows and pigs.
Я человек со своей гражданской позицией.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Everything according to...' Barinov answers sharply toward Kostya, testing Kostya's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
'Get out of here.' Kostya proceeds decisively at once and puts the weight on "poshel" ("go, off you go", from "poyti") as the exchange unfolds.
'Exactly.' Leaning in calmly before Kostya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Wait, are you upset?' Kostya questions firmly where this conversation is heading next.
'No, not really.' Barinov gently chooses this direct affirmation while facing Kostya using "da" ("yes") — a crisp "da" ("yes") that confirms the point without extra words.
'That means you are upset.' Holding firm briskly with Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'He is still my dad, after all.' Barinov opens up steadily with a smile, making his position completely clear.
'Why did the two of you have a falling-out anyway?' Kostya continues warmly during the talk and puts the weight on "porugalis" ("to quarrel", from "porugatsya") as the exchange unfolds.
'Those are cows and pigs.' Discussing the cow right here, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'I hate what happens to them.' Kostya cuts in candidly beside Barinov, so Barinov knows he is not just making small talk.
'Mom, I am not a child anymore.' Bringing up a child at once, Barinov brings in "rebyonok" ("a child") to make the meaning unmistakable.
Я человек со своей гражданской позицией.
'I am a person with my own civic stance.' Insisting on how civil he is beside Barinov, Kostya links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Well, listen here, person.' Barinov proceeds quietly beside Kostya, refusing to let the moment slip past.
Я человек со своей гражданской позицией.
That wraps up this scene as nastya explains to Kostya that she left home because her father owns a meatpacking plant and mocked her vegetarian principles. See you next time!
